A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReCALL framework and retain matching core experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections 6–8.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIRR and FashionIQ retrieval results, mining and component ablations, backbone comparisons and qualitative retrieval examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds scaling, transfer, model-capacity and human triplet-validation results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The adaptation, failure mining, CoT-based minimal editing, VQA filtering and grouped refinement pipeline remains unchanged, including the InfoNCE-plus-triplet objective. The supplement documents prompts and evaluates variants without establishing a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIRR and FashionIQ for composed image retrieval. The supplementary studies examine the same benchmark data and generated triplets; additional backbones, parameter settings and quality checks do not introduce a new retrieval domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. v2 adds CIRR comparisons against Random Mining and Hard Neg. Mining (No Edit) in Table 7; v1's mining comparison covered Random Mining on FashionIQ only.

E3.justification: Primary benchmark protocols remain stable, but the supplement adds substantial experimental designs: K=1–5 scaling without VQA filtering and using InfoNCE, a loss-weight/margin grid, LLaVA-NeXT transfer settings, larger LoRA ranks and full fine-tuning, and three human evaluators checking 300 filtered triplets.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's mining/component ablations and Qwen backbone comparison, v2 adds data-scale and hyperparameter sensitivity studies, computational analysis, cross-family transfer, direct hard-negative and capacity controls, and human validation of filtering. Sections 8.1–8.3 also add retrieval, synthesis and failure-case analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report four-seed means and standard deviations for Random Mining in Table 3. The new studies provide point estimates without additional repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or inter-rater agreement statistics.

E6.justification: Main-table results remain unchanged, including ReCALL's CIRR R@1 of 55.52% and FashionIQ average R@10 of 57.04%. Substantial new results include LLaVA R@1 of 51.93% baseline, 53.08% with transferred data and 54.65% with the full pipeline, plus scaling, sensitivity, capacity, runtime and 92% human-validated triplet accuracy results.

T1.justification: The task formulation and loss equations (1)–(3) retain their mathematical content. The supplement adds empirical analyses and qualitative reasoning, without new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: retrieval adaptation degrades native compositional reasoning, the model-agnostic ReCALL pipeline recalibrates it, and ReCALL achieves state-of-the-art CIRR/FashionIQ performance. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning shared versus model-specific blind spots, semantic correction versus negative repulsion, capacity-related overfitting and distribution preservation. Unlike v1's success-focused discussion, Section 8.3 examines sparse annotations, ambiguous instructions and residual spatial-rotation failures, including possible inherited backbone weaknesses.

D1.justification: v2 supplies full retrieval, verification and generation prompts, structured output requirements, a filtering confidence threshold, and stage-specific runtime and generated/retained sample counts. Its abstract also replaces the promised future code release with a stated repository address. These substantially extend v1's implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including TRACE, TiGER and WISER, and removes Anwaar et al.'s compositional-learning reference. The relationship to prior MLLM retrieval and self-improvement work remains substantially unchanged; many other reference edits concern metadata or duplicate consolidation.

P1.justification: The retained narrative receives grammar edits, more consistent informative-instance terminology and a shortened conclusion, while Sections 1–5 preserve their organization. Author/affiliation details and acknowledgments change. New supplementary sections organize added material rather than substantially restructuring the original argument.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–8 and Figures 5–15, including scaling plots, a sensitivity heatmap, prompt panels, retrieval failures and synthesis walkthroughs. The original backbone and qualitative figures are retained but renumbered and relocated from the references area into the experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves evidential support and reproducibility through direct mining/capacity controls, cross-family transfer, human validation, full prompts, cost reporting and explicit failure analysis. These address important omissions in v1 without relying on higher headline scores. Some causal explanations remain inferential, and the new FashionIQ filtering count is inconsistent: Section 6.3 reports 5,947 removals, whereas Table 5 implies 5,970. These limitations do not outweigh the gains.
